title: Quantum Quill
summary: A dependable place to plan a story, build its world, and keep writing. Novel writing comes first; the foundations should also serve other kinds of storytelling.
validation: The alpha preparation passed 383 tests across 37 suites, TypeScript, and the production build locally on October 24. A clean production-only install also passed fresh database initialization, account isolation, conflict, restart, export and paired restore checks. Live Render verification remains pending.

attention.label: Getting ready for testers

attention.title: Keep legacy conversion deliberate
attention.text: Four older entries still need a destination decision; two classification conflicts and orphan planning records remain preserved. Compatibility reads work. No destructive migration is approved.

attention.label: Scope matters

features.title: Writing you can recover
features.summary: Keep drafts through failed saves and reloads, with explicit choices when another tab or device has newer writing.
scope: Account/project-scoped durable draft journals and serialized autosave.
Server revisions, restore/discard review and protected navigation/export.
features.boundary: Draft recovery is implemented. It is not full offline app loading or a complete version-history browser.
features.acceptance: Offline edits remain recoverable; reconnect cannot silently replace newer server writing; switching accounts cannot reveal another account's drafts.
features.evidence: docs/DRAFT_RECOVERY_AND_DATA_INTEGRITY.md; save, recovery and conflict suites

features.title: One dependable data contract
features.summary: Use shared validation and classification while retaining every original field and legacy payload.
scope: Shared catalog, type-specific validation and compatibility readers are in place.
Versioned v2 documents and a disposable migration/rollback rehearsal are prepared.
features.boundary: 47 recovered records and 828 audited field paths were retained in rehearsal. Activation and ambiguous conversions have not been applied.
features.acceptance: Each recovered field has a documented destination or retained payload; reviewed migration and rollback preserve counts and values.
features.evidence: docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md; docs/DATA_CONTRACT_REHEARSAL.md

features.title: Relationships that stay connected
features.summary: Connect all seven entry types by identity, with roles, context, dates and useful backlinks.
scope: Shared searchable relationship picker, safe stubs and current target names.
Event participation/consequences, group membership, location governance/history and world-element usage/references.
features.boundary: Same-project validation, hierarchy cycle checks and archive/delete guards work. A visual graph is a separate later feature.
features.acceptance: Create, edit, remove and rename-target round trips retain meaning; invalid targets/cycles are rejected; linked deletion has predictable behavior.
features.evidence: docs/SHARED_RELATIONSHIPS.md; relationship API and field suites

features.title: Start with a little guidance
features.summary: Use the New Project and Blueprint wizards, or skip planning and go straight to writing.
scope: Recoverable New Project Wizard and restored Blueprint Wizard.
Create project structure and scenes without replacing existing prose.
features.boundary: The restored flows work; future guidance improvements should reuse their protected drafts.
features.acceptance: Wizard progress is recoverable and repeatable; direct-to-writing remains a first-class path.
features.evidence: docs/WIZARDS_AND_SCENES.md; later stabilization closeout supersedes its old limitations

features.title: From plot point to prose
features.summary: Move from Storyboard plot points to Outline scenes, scene story beats and manuscript writing.
scope: Scene planning and story beats connect the Storyboard, Outline and Write workflows.
Existing outline notes and chapter-only writing remain available.
features.boundary: Planning is optional. The complete journey still needs more sustained real-project usability testing.
features.acceptance: A writer can start at any stage, follow a planned scene into Write and retain plans separately from prose.
features.evidence: docs/SCENE_OUTLINE_WORKFLOW.md; planning and scene-beat tests

features.title: Shape the manuscript safely
features.summary: Reorder chapters and scenes, move scenes between chapters, and keep their writing intact.
scope: Persisted chapter/scene ordering with atomic moves and stale-arrangement checks.
Safe chapter rename/completion and guarded chapter deletion.
features.boundary: Scene deletion and automatic conversion between chapter writing modes are not exposed.
features.acceptance: Moving/reordering preserves prose, scene plans and references; conflicting arrangements are rejected without partial updates.
features.evidence: docs/STABILIZATION_CLOSEOUT.md; manuscript API and PostgreSQL rehearsal

features.title: A writer's formatting toolkit
features.summary: Use fonts, rich formatting and reusable Quill styles without giving up protected saves.
scope: Font/size, headings, emphasis, color, paragraph controls, lists, tables, images and find/replace.
Premade typographic styles and account-level custom saved styles.
features.boundary: This is not a paginated publishing engine. Footnotes, headers/footers and tracked changes remain outside the current editor.
features.acceptance: Formatting and custom styles survive save/reload, export within documented limits and draft recovery.
features.evidence: docs/WRITE_FORMATTING.md; formatting, style and export tests

features.title: Give the prose room
features.summary: Keep prose central, with a compact manuscript navigator and separate scene/context panes.
scope: Shared workspace navigation and a responsive, single-row formatting bar.
Reserved save-status space and context panels that preserve editor state.
A discreet roadmap link in workspace navigation and the dashboard sidebar opens a separate tab without leaving the writing session.
features.boundary: Broader browser, mobile and input-method testing is still needed before a release claim.
features.acceptance: Opening cards or plans does not push prose down, reset the editor or remove formatting tools.
features.evidence: docs/WORKSPACE_INTEGRATION.md; workspace writing tests and fixture walkthrough; October 23 roadmap shortcut (0067b97): type check, production build and browser walkthrough

features.title: A readable Story Bible library
features.summary: Find an entry and work in a focused detail pane instead of navigating oversized category dashboards.
scope: Seven types, search, filters, stars, archive and sorting.
Overview, Develop, Connections and preserved imported Source views.
features.boundary: Type-specific editors remain complete, but more field guidance and a guided creation journey are still needed.
features.acceptance: Filters persist, narrow screens have clear navigation, every field remains available and tab changes preserve unsaved edits.
features.evidence: docs/STORY_BIBLE_WORKSPACE.md; library and mounted-editor tests

features.title: Keep the world beside the writing
features.summary: Link elements inline and use interactive cards without leaving the Write workspace.
scope: Type @ or link selected words; pin viewpoint, cast, locations and references to a scene.
Open facts, relationships and scene notes; edit the full entry in place.
features.boundary: Renaming an entry updates its card, not the author's words. Inline mentions and scene pins remain separate connections.
features.acceptance: Card edits and prose save independently; links survive undo, formatting and recovery; foreign targets are rejected.
features.evidence: docs/WORKSPACE_INTEGRATION.md; docs/SCENE_STORY_BIBLE.md

features.title: Find missing scene connections
features.summary: Scan the current scene for mentions of existing entries, then review what should be connected.
scope: Read live prose, including unsaved text; show excerpts and flag ambiguous names.
Default to a mentioned reference; the writer may choose cast or setting before adding.
features.boundary: Current scene only. Literal name/alias matching, not semantic inference. No new entries, automatic linking or prose edits.
features.acceptance: Linked/archived/foreign entries are excluded, stale scans require review, and approved connections use the existing protected save queue.
features.evidence: docs/SCENE_STORY_BIBLE.md, October 14 addition; 380 tests / 36 suites recorded

features.title: Bring the original story across
features.summary: Use a preserved Notion import as a realistic test of the entire writing organizer.
scope: 39 Bible entries, 29 chapters, 60 scene records, 29 plot points and 93 scene beats imported into a separate project.
233 scene connections across 60 records; source material and images retained.
features.boundary: This is a reviewed one-story import, not ongoing Notion sync. Thirteen Bible entries are archived examples/templates. One long chapter draft intentionally remains intact.
features.acceptance: Existing projects and source records remain unchanged; imports and context links retain prose/formatting byte for byte.
features.evidence: docs/NOTION_WORLD_BIBLE_IMPORT.md covers the first phase; private manuscript/context import receipts cover later phases

features.title: Take your manuscript with you
features.summary: Export real Word, HTML, plain text, EPUB and original-record JSON files.
scope: Manuscript-order exports, optional planning/Bible content and authorized local images.
Preview with browser Print / Save PDF; pending writes and unresolved drafts are guarded.
features.boundary: The exports work. External EPUB validation, broader reader checks and complex publishing-layout fidelity remain open; PDF is a browser print flow.
features.acceptance: Export includes the latest saved writing in order, preserves supported formatting and has reviewed limits for each target format.
features.evidence: docs/STABILIZATION_CLOSEOUT.md; binary export and snapshot tests

features.title: A more guided Story Bible
features.summary: Make it obvious what each element is for, which fields matter first, and how to develop it.
scope: Explain purpose and show examples for all seven types, inspired by the WBB workflow.
Separate essential facts from optional depth; suggest relevant next connections.
features.boundary: Existing forms and basic guidance work. The complete guided entry-creation experience is not yet implemented.
features.acceptance: A new writer can create and develop an element without guessing field meaning; every existing field, link and recovered original still round-trips.
features.evidence: User-approved direction; docs/ANTIGRAVITY_STORY_BIBLE_INTEGRATION.md

features.title: Develop characters with intention
features.summary: Connect character goals, needs, beliefs, conflicts and change to their role in the story.
scope: A guided character workbench using existing facts and retained imported prompts.
Useful references and arc prompts connected to scenes and events.
features.boundary: Current character fields already store much of this material. The proposed workbench must not create a second competing data model.
features.acceptance: Existing character data appears in the guided experience without duplication; prompts are optional and edits remain recoverable.
features.evidence: Antigravity comparison and WBB-inspired product direction; implementation not started

features.title: See the story's chronology
features.summary: Arrange events over time while respecting fictional calendars, approximate dates and uncertainty.
scope: Define date/order rules before adding a timeline view.
Use existing event relationships and distinguish story chronology from manuscript order.
features.boundary: Event dates and timeline flags currently store intent; no complete timeline screen or fictional-calendar ordering exists.
features.acceptance: Uncertain dates remain uncertain, calendars have explicit ordering rules, and links open the underlying event/scene without copied names.
features.evidence: docs/STORY_BIBLE_ROADMAP.md, remaining section workflows

features.title: A writer's knowledge organizer
features.summary: Collect research and connect useful knowledge to the world and the writing it informs.
scope: Current Research entries support sources, summaries, topics, notes, next steps and links.
Extend toward richer notes, quotations, attachments and deliberate application to story elements.
features.boundary: Basic Research entries work. A complete knowledge library, attachment workflows, reminders and cross-project reuse are not built.
features.acceptance: Sources stay traceable, quotes and author notes remain distinct, attachments recover cleanly after failures, and applying research never silently overwrites fiction.
features.evidence: Current Research editor; docs/STORY_BIBLE_ROADMAP.md and user product vision

features.title: Review connections across a project
features.summary: Extend the scene scanner into a manageable review across a longer manuscript.
scope: Project-wide review with progress, scene context and explicit alias management.
Keep ambiguous names and possible new entries as separate decisions.
features.boundary: The approved first version matches existing entries one scene at a time. New-entry suggestions would be a further scope decision.
features.acceptance: Review resumes safely, ignores stale results, avoids duplicates and applies only chosen links without editing prose.
features.evidence: Follow-up to the existing-entry scanner; not implemented

features.title: Review the remaining legacy mappings
features.summary: Resolve ambiguous recovered records before activating structured conversions.
scope: Review four lore/timeline records and two classification conflicts.
Keep orphan planning records and all original payloads until their meaning is established.
features.boundary: Preview and disposable rehearsal exist. No destructive production conversion is approved; this does not block normal writing through compatibility readers.
features.acceptance: Each mapping has a reviewed preview, retained original, equal before/after counts and values, and a rehearsed rollback.
features.evidence: docs/DATA_CONTRACT_REHEARSAL.md; 47 records / 828 audited field paths

features.title: Reusable, reviewable imports
features.summary: Turn the successful one-story import into a clear workflow other projects can use.
scope: Preview mappings, examples/templates, duplicates, images and manuscript boundaries.
Support safe retries and retain source provenance and original payloads.
features.boundary: Import scripts and preserved receipts exist. There is no general import UI or live Notion synchronization.
features.acceptance: A preview explains every destination; retries cannot duplicate records; failures roll back cleanly and prose stays unchanged unless explicitly transformed.
features.evidence: Existing world-bible import/rehearsal provides the foundation; reusable UI not started

features.title: A sustained real-story walkthrough
features.summary: Use the imported novel to find friction across planning, writing, world-building and export.
scope: Follow a real chapter through every relevant workspace, including long forms and manuscript navigation.
Broaden keyboard, compact-screen, browser and input-method checks while retaining the fixture suite.
features.boundary: Focused synthetic and imported-project walkthroughs passed. Everyday multi-session use and broad device coverage remain open.
features.acceptance: Critical tasks are clear without coaching, prose keeps its space, and navigation/reload/failure cases retain writing and context.
features.evidence: Existing integration reports document limited walkthroughs; this is the next wider acceptance pass

features.title: Publishing quality you can check
features.summary: Validate longer manuscripts and realistic formatting in the tools readers and writers actually use.
scope: External EPUB validation/reader checks and representative Word/HTML/print review.
Document fonts, lists, tables, images and supported publishing-layout limits.
features.boundary: Real export is already delivered. This milestone validates quality and resolves observed defects; it does not promise a full desktop publishing engine.
features.acceptance: Representative exports open correctly, retain content/order and pass agreed format checks with visible limitations.
features.evidence: docs/STABILIZATION_CLOSEOUT.md, publishing QA boundaries

features.title: An open alpha on Render
features.summary: Prepare a separate hosted app where testers can register their own accounts and try Quantum Quill.
scope: Open registration selected. Dedicated app, PostgreSQL database and persistent uploads are prepared; recovered manuscripts stay local.
Fresh-database and production-runtime rehearsal covers saves, conflicts, account isolation, restart persistence and paired restore.
Use the confirmed Render workspace when launch is authorized; publish the tester link only after live verification.
features.boundary: Deployment preparation is checked locally; launch is on hold and no live tester URL exists. Hosting has not been activated. Upstream editor/validation dependency upgrades remain tracked with scoped safeguards.
features.acceptance: Staging passes real writer flows and account isolation; database/uploads restore is proven; costs and rollback are reviewed before release.
features.evidence: docs/HOSTED_ALPHA.md; user requested a shareable alpha and open registration on October 24

features.title: Write with a full offline workspace
features.summary: Go beyond durable draft recovery so the application itself can reopen without a network connection.
scope: Define secure offline caching and account-scoped local availability.
Resume sync with explicit conflict handling and clear storage limits.
features.boundary: Offline drafts are protected today if the app loads. Full offline loading and a complete version-history browser are not implemented.
features.acceptance: The app loads offline, account changes never expose another account's content, and reconnect preserves newer writing on both sides.
features.evidence: Explicit future boundary in recovery and workspace reports

features.title: Share and collaborate deliberately
features.summary: Invite readers or collaborators with clear access and safe editing behavior.
scope: Define roles, invitations and project/file access before enabling sharing.
Plan history and collaborative editing separately from today's conflict review.
features.boundary: Sharing is labeled as planned in the app. Current revision checks are not multiplayer editing or collaborator permissions.
features.acceptance: Access can be granted/revoked predictably, private files remain protected, and concurrent edits cannot silently lose writing.
features.evidence: Deferred product scope; no delivery date or implementation claim

features.title: Explore the world as a graph
features.summary: Explore established relationships visually once the library, backlinks and chronology are useful.
scope: Navigate the shared ID-based links with filters and readable context.
Keep the existing list/picker interfaces usable without the graph.
features.boundary: Relationships and backlinks already work. A graph view and the legacy whiteboard are not active features.
features.acceptance: The graph reads the same link model, stays navigable on large projects and never becomes the only way to edit connections.
features.evidence: Deferred after shared relationships and chronology

features.title: Optional story assistance
features.summary: Explore assistance that supports the writer's decisions without taking ownership of the story.
scope: Begin with explicit, reviewable use cases and data/privacy choices.
Separate suggestions from authored facts and manuscript text.
features.boundary: No external AI generation or semantic scanner is active. Existing connection scanning is local name matching.
features.acceptance: Suggestions are opt-in, explain their basis and never overwrite prose or establish story facts automatically.
features.evidence: Later exploration, not a scheduled implementation

features.title: Beyond the novel
features.summary: Adapt the writing organizer for RPG campaigns, scripts, plays and historical storytelling.
scope: Identify the shared world, scene, reference and planning capabilities.
Add format-specific workflows only after testing them with real examples.
features.boundary: Novel writing is the current focus. These formats are product possibilities, not supported end-to-end workflows today.
features.acceptance: Each new format has a demonstrated complete workflow without complicating or weakening novel writing.
features.evidence: User's long-term product vision

projectNotes: Later: reconstruct the history of Quantum Quill from its surviving versions, archives and development records. This is a separate storytelling project, not a prerequisite for the alpha.
October 23: public GitHub Pages roadmap published; eight actual-app screenshots prepared using original fictional sample content for alpha recruitment. The application itself remains a local alpha.

October 24: public GitHub introduction, actual-app screenshots and tester feedback guide published. Open-registration Render alpha is prepared and locally checked; launch is on hold. No live app URL is advertised before verification.
